style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: 'The LORD reigns' -- the shortest of the enthronement psalms and the loudest, five verses that put the whole sea against the whole God. He has dressed for His session, robed in majesty and belted in strength, and because He reigns the world stands and will not be shaken; His throne has stood since 'then,' whenever then was, and He Himself is from everlasting. Then the challenge: the floods have lifted up, lifted up their voice, lift up their pounding -- the chaos-waters that Canaanite myth made a rival god, given a voice three times over. And the answer, in one line: louder than the voice of many waters, mightier than the sea's mighty breakers, the LORD on high is mighty. The same word for the waves and for God, and the comparison settles it. The last verse turns from the sea to the sanctuary: His testimonies are utterly sure, and holiness befits His house for length of days -- because a King who rules the ocean also rules by a word, and His house has a standard.

1.text: The LORD reigns! He has clothed Himself in majesty; the LORD has clothed Himself, has belted Himself with strength. Yes, the world is set firm; it cannot be shaken.
1.amp: The LORD [YHWH] reigns [malak], He is clothed [labash] with majesty [geut]; the LORD is clothed with strength [oz], wherewith He has girded [azar -- belted] Himself: the world [tebel] also is stablished [kun], that it cannot be moved [mot].
1.notes: YHWH malakh (H3068, H4427): 'the LORD reigns' -- the cry of the enthronement psalms (93:1, 96:10, 97:1, 99:1; cf. 47:8, 'God reigneth'), possibly the shout with which the ark was carried up. geut labesh (H1348, H3847), labesh YHWH oz hitazzar (H5797, H247): robed in majesty, belted in strength -- a King dressing for His session. aph-tikkon tebel bal-timmot (H3559, H8398, H4131): and INDEED (aph, 'also, yea' -- here carrying the force of consequence) the world stands; creation's stability is a function of His reign.

2.text: Your throne stands established from of old; You are from everlasting.
2.amp: Your throne [kisse] is established [kun] of old ['from then', az, the KJV margin]: You are from everlasting [olam].
2.notes: nakhon kisakha me-az (H3559, H3678, H227): the throne set firm by the same establishing-verb as the world in verse 1 -- me-az, 'from then', the margin's literal: from the beginning, whenever that was. me-olam attah (H5769): You are from everlasting -- the throne is old; the King is older.

3.text: The rivers have lifted up, O LORD -- the rivers have lifted their voice; the rivers lift up their crashing surge.
3.amp: The floods [nahar -- rivers, floods] have lifted up [nasa], O LORD [YHWH], the floods have lifted up their voice [qol]; the floods lift up their waves [doki -- their pounding, their crashing].
3.notes: naseu neharot YHWH (H5375, H5104): the rivers have LIFTED UP -- three times, staircase parallelism -- qolam (H6963), their voice, then dokhyam (H1796), their pounding: the sea-chaos that pagan myth made a rival god, given a voice and a fist. The threat is real and loud.

4.text: Louder than the sound of many waters, mightier than the mighty breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty.
4.amp: The LORD [YHWH] on high [marom] is mightier [addir -- majestic, mighty] than the noise [qol] of many [rav] waters [mayim], yea, than the mighty [addir] waves [mishbar -- breakers] of the sea [yam].
4.notes: mi-qolot mayim rabbim (H6963, H4325, H7227): more than the voices of many waters -- addirim mishbere-yam (H117, H4867, H3220): the MIGHTY breakers of the sea -- addir ba-marom YHWH (H4791, H3068): MIGHTY on high is the LORD. The same word, addir, for the waves and for God; the comparison settles who is more so. Revelation 19:6 turns the image round: the voice 'as the voice of many waters' is the great multitude crying 'the Lord God omnipotent reigneth' -- verse 1's shout, now on the lips of the redeemed.

5.text: Your testimonies are utterly sure; holiness is fitting for Your house, O LORD, for length of days.
5.amp: Your testimonies [edah] are very [meod] sure [aman -- firm, trustworthy]: holiness [qodesh] becomes [naah -- befits] Your house [bayith], O LORD [YHWH], for ever ['to length of days', orek yamim, the KJV margin].
5.notes: edotekha neemnu meod (H5713, H539, H3966): the King who rules the sea also rules by testimonies -- neemnu, from aman, 'to be firm, trustworthy', and meod, VERY: utterly sure. le-betekha naavah-qodesh YHWH (H1004, H4998, H6944): holiness befits Your house -- cognate with naveh, 'comely', in Psalm 33:1 -- le-orekh yamim (H753, H3117), the margin's 'to length of days'. Power over chaos, and a holy house: the two sides of the reign.
